title: Ciox Health Reviews (2026): What Legal Teams Should Know Before Choosing a Medical Record Retrieval Partner
summary: Ciox Health reviews for 2026: BBB ratings, settlements, the 2024 data incident, fees, and how Codes Health compares for plaintiff law firms.
body_markdown:
For plaintiff law firms handling personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice cases, medical record retrieval is the foundation of case development. Delays, incomplete records, and unpredictable fees can throw off case timelines and add to operating costs. Many legal teams have worked with Ciox Health, a long-established release-of-information company that now operates as part of Datavant. This review looks at Ciox Health's history, customer feedback, legal track record, and fee considerations so litigation teams can make an informed decision about whether it fits their needs or whether an[AI-powered retrieval partner](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) offers a better path forward.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Ciox Health (now Datavant) holds a[1/5 customer review average](https://www.bbb.org/us/ga/alpharetta/profile/health-and-wellness/datavant-formally-ciox-health-0443-27163823/customer-reviews) on BBB from 32 reviews, with 48 complaints logged over the past three years. Its separate BBB business rating is B-.


-


Ciox agreed to a[$1.85 million settlement](https://www.beckershospitalreview.com/legal-regulatory-issues/ciox-health-pays-1-85m-to-resolve-claims-it-overcharges-patients-for-ehr-records/) resolving Texas allegations that it charged fees above state limits. Ciox denied wrongdoing.


-


A May 2024 phishing incident was reported to HHS as affecting 320,702 individuals, and a[$900,000 class settlement](https://www.hipaajournal.com/datavant-group-class-action-data-breach-settlement/) covering about 58,309 people received final approval in September 2026.


-


Datavant now markets a legal and insurance offering with AI-powered summaries, analysis, and chronologies, so the real comparison comes down to specific workflow differences.


-


Retrieval charges can vary by request type, state law, delivery method, and contract terms, while Codes Health uses flat-fee pricing.


-


Codes Health works toward complete records in a couple of weeks, with AI review before submission, Missing Record Review, and potential breaches of care flagged for attorney review.


-


Codes Health says same-day retrieval services often return incomplete record sets that need added client involvement, which can lead to client churn.


## **Understanding Ciox Health's Role in Medical Records Retrieval**


Ciox Health[launched in 2016](https://www.healthcareitnews.com/news/healthport-iod-care-communications-ecs-merge-new-company-ciox-health) following the combination of HealthPort, IOD, Care Communications, and ECS. Its corporate lineage through HealthPort dates to 1976. Ciox merged with Datavant in 2021, and the business now operates under the Datavant name.


Historically, Ciox's work has centered on healthcare operations such as:


-


Medicare Advantage risk adjustment services


-


Health plan chart retrieval


-


On-site hospital ROI teams


-


Enterprise healthcare data operations


Today, Datavant also markets a dedicated legal and insurance offering for law firms, insurers, and TPAs. It covers record retrieval, record discovery, AI-powered summaries and chronologies, and medical expert review. So for plaintiff firms, the question isn't whether Datavant serves legal teams. It's which specific workflows matter most for your cases, and how each vendor handles authorization quality, record completeness, pricing, and fit with your case management system.


## **What Customer Reviews Reveal About Ciox Health**


On BBB, where the company is listed as Datavant (formerly Ciox Health), it holds a[1/5 customer review average](https://www.bbb.org/us/ga/alpharetta/profile/health-and-wellness/datavant-formally-ciox-health-0443-27163823/customer-reviews) based on 32 reviews. That figure is the customer review average, not BBB's business rating, which is currently B-.


### **Common Themes in Customer Reviews**


**Payment and processing delays:**


-


"Still waiting for payment for charts that were already uploaded over a month ago"


-


"Everytime I call, I get, 'I will send an email.' Again, nothing ever gets done"


**Hard-to-reach customer support:**


-


"Impossible to reach someone on the phone"


-


Multiple reviews mention difficulty connecting with representatives


**Retrieval workflow frustrations:**


-


"Medical records retrieval system is beyond ridiculous"


-


"Don't think I've ever actually been able to request records and receive them successfully in the 5 to 6 years I've been forced to call them"


**Communication concerns:**


-


Complaints about "insecure email communications and cumbersome retrieval workflows"


BBB shows[48 total complaints](https://www.bbb.org/us/ga/alpharetta/profile/health-and-wellness/datavant-formally-ciox-health-0443-27163823/complaints) over the past three years, with 19 complaints closed in the last 12 months. The company is not BBB accredited.


For litigation teams working under strict deadlines, reviewer-reported experiences like these are worth weighing alongside a vendor's own published service claims.


## **Ciox Health's Legal and Compliance Track Record**


Beyond customer reviews, Ciox Health has been involved in several legal and regulatory matters. Each one involved allegations, and the settlements below did not include an admission of the underlying wrongdoing.


### **$1.85 Million Texas Fee Settlement**


Ciox Health agreed to a[$1.85 million settlement](https://www.beckershospitalreview.com/legal-regulatory-issues/ciox-health-pays-1-85m-to-resolve-claims-it-overcharges-patients-for-ehr-records/) resolving allegations that it charged certain Texas requesters fees exceeding applicable limits. Plaintiffs alleged that one requester was charged $77.50, where they contended the applicable amount was $25. Ciox denied wrongdoing.


### **May 2024 Data Incident**


A phishing attack on May 8 to 9, 2024, led to unauthorized access to an email account. Ciox[reported the incident](https://www.hipaajournal.com/datavant-group-class-action-data-breach-settlement/) to HHS as affecting 320,702 individuals. Information that may have been exposed includes names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, and protected health information. The subsequent settlement class consists of approximately 58,309 people whose information may have been compromised. Ciox agreed to a $900,000 settlement, which received final approval in September 2026.


### **NOSSCR Complaint**


On March 25, 2024, the National Organization of Social Security Claimants' Representatives[filed a formal complaint](https://nosscr.org/article/nosscr-files-complaint-against-ciox-health-alleging-excessive-fees-and-more/) with HHS's Office for Civil Rights. NOSSCR alleged that Ciox required prepayment, charged excessive fees, and delayed providing records. These remain NOSSCR's allegations, not a government finding against Ciox.


## **Understanding Retrieval Fees and Cost Predictability**


Medical record charges can be hard to predict. A law firm blog post from Avard Law reproduces what appear to be[Ciox contractual terms](https://avardlaw.com/social-security-disability/ciox-health-medical-records-provider-trying-to-circumvent-hipaa-rules-for-fees/) listing potential charges such as:


-


Copying fees


-


Handling fees


-


Certification fees


-


Electronic data storage fees


-


"No record found" fees


That list is not a current official Datavant rate card, and these charges don't necessarily apply to every patient, attorney, facility, or jurisdiction. What a firm actually pays can depend on the request type, applicable state law, delivery method, custodian or provider charges, and contractual terms.


Patient access requests work differently, too. HHS explains that a[$6.50 flat fee](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/is-650-the-maximum-amount-that-can-be-charged/index.html) is just one optional method for calculating charges on certain electronic patient requests, not a universal fee or cap.


Codes Health takes a simpler approach: flat-fee pricing with no per-page charges, so firms know their retrieval costs upfront. For practices handling high case volumes, predictable pricing makes case economics much easier to plan.


## **Turnaround Time: Why Speed and Completeness Both Matter**


Turnaround depends on the provider, the request type, the quality of the authorization, and the retrieval channel, so timelines vary across vendors and individual requests. Before signing on with any vendor, Datavant, ask for documentation of current turnaround on legal requests similar to yours.


Slow or incomplete retrieval creates real bottlenecks for litigation teams:


-


**Pre-litigation evaluation delays:** Cases can't be properly valued without complete medical records


-


**Statute of limitations pressure:** Slow retrieval compresses the time available for case development


-


**Expert witness scheduling:** Medical experts can't begin review until records arrive


-


**Demand preparation setbacks:** Strong demands require complete documentation


-


**Settlement negotiation disadvantages:** Incomplete records weaken negotiating positions


Speed alone isn't the whole story, though. Codes Health notes that services advertising same-day retrieval often return only the records that are immediately available, leaving gaps that need additional client involvement to fill. In Codes Health's experience, that back-and-forth leads to client churn. Codes Health works toward complete records in a couple of weeks, not months, and checks deliveries against the original request before closing them out. That helps legal teams:


-


Evaluate case merit faster


-


Identify missing records earlier in the process


-


Begin expert review sooner


-


Prepare demands with complete documentation


-


Maintain stronger negotiating positions

## **Authorization Quality Review: Preventing Costly Delays**


Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied record requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can force you to resubmit and start over. Common errors that trigger rejections include:


-


Missing patient signatures


-


Unclear or expired authorization dates


-


Unchecked boxes for sensitive records (mental health, substance abuse, HIV)


-


Misspelled patient or provider names


-


Incorrect dates of service


-


Missing provider-specific requirements


A rejected or defective authorization can force a request to be resubmitted and significantly delay processing. Applicable deadlines depend on the request type and jurisdiction. For example, HIPAA's right of access generally gives covered entities 30 days to respond to an individual's request, with state variations, while attorney-authorized requests may follow different procedures.


[Codes Health's AI review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) catches these errors before submission. The system automatically flags misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


Datavant also documents authorization validation controls, although its public materials don't clearly describe the same requester-side, pre-submission error-checking workflow.
